note: Source's 'I hope... or let any feeling linger' became a flat exhortation 'Nor should', dropping the hope.
replacement: “There is one principle, Athenians, that I hold to through everything: no concession to the Peloponnesians. I know that the spirit that inspires men while they are being persuaded to make war is not always kept once they act, and that resolutions change as circumstances change. Yet I see that now, as before, the same counsel is demanded of me, almost literally the same. And I put it to those of you who are allowing yourselves to be persuaded: support the national resolves even if we meet with reverses, or else give up all credit for their wisdom if we succeed. For sometimes the course of events is as arbitrary as the plans of men; indeed this is why we usually blame chance for whatever does not happen as we expected. Now it was clear before that Lacedaemon entertained designs against us, and it is still clearer now. The treaty provides that we shall submit our differences to each other for legal settlement and that meanwhile each shall keep what it has. Yet the Lacedaemonians have never made us any such offer and have never accepted one from us. On the contrary, they wish complaints to be settled by war instead of by negotiation, and in the end we find them here dropping the tone of expostulation and adopting that of command. They order us to raise the siege of Potidæa, to let Aegina be independent, and to revoke the Megara decree, and they conclude with an ultimatum warning us to leave the Hellenes independent. I hope none of you will think that we shall be going to war for a trifle if we refuse to revoke the Megara decree. It stands in front of their complaints, and its revocation is supposed to save us from war. I hope, too, that no feeling of self-reproach will linger in your minds, as if you went to war for slight cause. Why, this trifle contains the whole seal and trial of your resolution. If you give way, you will instantly have to meet some greater demand, since you will have been frightened into obedience in the first instance, whereas a firm refusal will make them understand clearly that they must treat you more as equals. Make your decision therefore at once: either submit before you are harmed, or, if we are to go to war, as I for one think we ought, do so without caring whether the ostensible cause is great or small, resolved against making concessions and against consenting to a precarious tenure of our possessions. For every claim from an equal, urged upon a neighbor as a command before any attempt at legal settlement, whether great or small, has only one meaning, and that is slavery.

note: Added connective 'So' that the source lacks.
replacement: These were the charges and differences between the rival powers before the war, which arose immediately from the affair at Epidamnus and Corcyra. Even so, intercourse and mutual communication went on. It was carried on without heralds, though not without suspicion, because events were happening that amounted to a breach of the treaty and gave grounds for war.
